messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: elevated error rate on continuous-batcher service (runtime-prod). 90th p50 latency spike, OOMs observed, 5xxs to customers. Incident severity: high. Thread started at 1749999999

mike-oncall: I'm on it. seeing batcher queue growth on multiple pods, GPU OOMs and container restarts. customer impact: a few high-traffic tenants seeing 502 / 10s latencies. Paging Eng-Run & SRE.

priya: ok. which nodes are flapping? any kdump / kernel OOM logs?

mike-oncall: quick snapshot:
```
# kubectl get pods -n runtime | grep continuous-batcher
continuous-batcher-7f9d4   2/2   Running   3 (1 Restart)   28m\ncontinuous-batcher-9c2a1   0/2   CrashLoopBackOff  5 (2 Restarts)  26m\ncontinuous-batcher-1a3b7   2/2   Running   0       2h

# kubectl describe pod continuous-batcher-9c2a1 -n runtime | tail -n 20
Last State:     Terminated\n  Reason:       OOMKilled\n  Exit Code:    137\n  Started:      Thu Mar 14 22:40:01 UTC 2024\n  Finished:     Thu Mar 14 22:41:02 UTC 2024
```

mike-oncall: tail of container logs shows CUDA OOM and batch growth loop:
```
E 03-14 22:40:00.123 main.cpp:456] Alloc failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (2)
W 03-14 22:40:00.124 batcher.cc:210] batch_size=24512 queue_length=12000 prefetch=on
E 03-14 22:40:00.125 runtime.cc:98] Unhandled exception: std::bad_alloc
```

alice: that batch_size in the logs looks wrong. default max should be ~4096. looks like accumulator didn't cap. could be prefetch + continuous growth bug.

brian: +1. we've seen accumulator drift when prefetch and kv-cache growth coincide. queue_length=12000 is panic level.

mike-oncall: mitigation steps I'm going to run now: 1) reduce prefetch to 0 via configmap for batchers, 2) set BATCHER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE env to 4096, 3) cordon/drain the most affected node to stop new pods landing. I'll post commands.

mike-oncall: (running)
```
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/continuous-batcher BATCHER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=4096
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/continuous-batcher PREFETCH_ENABLED=false
kubectl cordon gke-prod-runtime-pool-3
kubectl drain gke-prod-runtime-pool-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

tim-ops: FYI I'm standing by to reboot the node if needed. kernel logs show GPU driver restarts on that node.

deploy-bot: deploy continuous-batcher env update initiated by mike-oncall (rollout id: rb-20240314-01).

priya: good. also let's scale an extra 4 replicas as short-term capacity to smooth load while we heal.

mike-oncall: scaled to +4 replicas.

deploy-bot: rollout succeeded. all new pods reported Ready=2/2 within 70s.

alice: checking metrics – queue length trending down on new pods, but older pods still leaking memory. we should recycle CrashLoopBackOff pods after env change.

mike-oncall: restarting problem pods now: kubectl delete pod continuous-batcher-9c2a1 -n runtime

mike-oncall: pod restarted and came up healthy. logs show batch_size capped and no immediate CUDA OOM.

sasha: from CS: affected customers (account ids: acct-148, acct-221) reported degraded response times for ~14 minutes. one ticket elevated to priority by customer. I've notified them that we're mitigating and will follow up.

priya: handoff plan: I'm taking the overnight watch. actions for follow-up: 1) add a safety check in batcher that enforces accumulator guard rails (max bytes and per-request token limit), 2) add integration test that simulates prefetch + kv-cache growth and verifies no unbounded accumulation, 3) postmortem with timeline and customer impact, 4) add alert for queue_length > 2000 and per-pod memory growth rate.

brian: I'll own the code patch for the accumulator guard. will open PR with tests. estimated ETA: 6 hours.

mike-oncall: handoff to priya complete. my notes: root cause suspected: continuous-batcher accumulation bug triggered by aggressive prefetch + kv-cache eviction causing repeated requeueing and unbounded batch accumulation -> memory growth -> CUDA OOM -> container crash -> pod churn -> node GPU driver instability -> node flaps.

tim-ops: node gke-prod-runtime-pool-3 evidence: kernel logs show repeated GPU driver resets and then kubelet restarting containers. I've rebooted the node and left it cordoned until we confirm no further driver panics.

priya: I'll coordinate redeploy of guarded binary and the integration tests tomorrow. also we should backfill metrics to correlate per-tenant traffic patterns that triggered the growth.

mike-oncall: brief customer impact summary for page: ~3 tenants impacted with increased latency (5-20s) and transient 502s. total impacted requests ~2.3k. no data loss. CS notified.

sasha: passing to account managers. will send post-incident note once we have timeline.

brian: quick snippet of the config fix I plan to ship in PR: 
```
// guard in batch_accumulator.cc
if (accumulator.size_bytes() + incoming.size_bytes() > config.max_accumulator_bytes) {
  // flush partial batch and reject oversized request
  flush();
  return Status::ResourceExhausted("request too large for accumulator");
}
```

priya: also add runtime flag to disable prefetch temporarily, and a metric for accumulator_bytes.

mike-oncall: closing loop: incident-bot has been notified that metrics returned to baseline and no new OOMs in the last 15m. uncordoning node gke-prod-runtime-pool-3.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: resolved by mitigations (config rollback/patch + pod restarts + node reboot). Severity downgraded to low.

mike-oncall: thanks team. handoff checklist in #incidents will reflect action items. Priya, please keep ops posted and file postmortem with owner tags.

priya: will do. I'll also schedule a quick runbook update to include immediate prefetch disable and max_batch env change as an emergency mitigation.

alice: one more note: let's add a canary that runs continuous-batcher under synthetic heavy prefetch to catch regressions in CI.

brian: agreed. opening PR now -> link will be posted in the follow-up.

sasha: customers updated. will follow up with account-specific notes once postmortem is drafted. :thumbsup:

mike-oncall: handing off final convo. good job everyone.
